newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bangladeshi dies in latest Bahrain arson attack.
newsitem.headline: Bangladeshi dies in latest Bahrain arson attack.

text.p: A Bangladeshi man was killed and another was seriously injured after arsonists set a store ablaze in Bahrain, a government official said on Sunday.
"A Bangladeshi was killed and another was in serious condition when a group attacked a cold store in Sitra on Saturday night," the official told Reuters.
The deadly attack was the latest in a series of arson attacks that have hit the island, the Gulf's main financial and banking centre.
"A group of people stormed the store and set it ablaze. Two Asians were inside the store which was completely gutted," Bahrain's official Gulf News Agency said.
Seven Bangladeshi workers died when suspected arsonists set a restaurant ablaze in Sitra, linked with the capital Manama by a three km (1.8 miles) causeway, in March 1996.
A power generator blew up at a luxury hotel in Manama on Saturday, causing a fire but there were no reports of damage or casualties, officials said.
Three fires rocked Muharraq, linked with Manama by another three km (1.8 miles) causeway, on Friday causing damage but there were no reports of casualties.

On Tuesday, an explosion hit a hotel in central Manama and witnesses said part of the roof of the hotel's nightclub had collapsed. A government official said initial reports indicated that a gas leak appeared to have caused the blast.
A series of arson attacks in early June were described by a government official as "continued acts of terrorism".

Members of the island's majority Shi'ite Moslem community have waged sporadic protests, bombings and arson attacks since December 1994 to press the Sunni-led government to introduce economic and political reforms.
Among the victims of the attacks have been members of Bahrain's Asian community, who some Bahrainis believe are taking away jobs and offer an easy target.
